## TL;DR

Task #1098’s implementation was already present on the branch when this recovery turn began. The queued handoff failure named one pressure-guard test on the ThinkPad host. I ran that test directly and it passed, then reran the required changed-path check. The first remote validation container hung and RepoOS removed it; a retry on Mini completed the build and all 303 changed/always-run test files successfully. The local contrast audit, UI smoke test, formatting, lint, build, and user-docs checks also passed. No source change was justified by the evidence, so the failure appears to have been transient host instability rather than a defect in the test or implementation.

## Work and rationale

I began by verifying the assigned absolute worktree, branch, task state, and handoff status. The branch was `feat/surface-why-an-agent-failed-expired-auth`, and RepoOS listed #1098 as active. The task specification and latest review report were present in this worktree. The review report said the classifier, failure presentation, notices, Agents last-run status, crash-recovery wording, tests, and docs met the feature requirements; its remaining concern was foreign task bookkeeping that RepoOS had already repaired in a prior branch commit. The latest handoff failure instead requested investigation of `waitForPressureRelief > waits until a fake probe reports relief, then proceeds` on ThinkPad.

I inspected the test and implementation. The test supplies a deterministic in-memory probe sequence and expects one wait notification before a relieved reading. The implementation enforces a 500 ms minimum poll interval, so the nominal `pollMs: 1` does not make it run instantly. Changing that production safeguard to accommodate a unit test would have been unjustified without a reproduced defect. I ran the focused Vitest case locally; it passed in about 506 ms. The test and production function are unchanged from main, further suggesting the failure was not introduced by this feature branch.

I then ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` as requested. Remote validation began on ThinkPad but eventually reported that its validation container was hung and removed it. RepoOS retried on Bee, where the incremental bundle could not be applied because the mirror lacked its base; RepoOS attempted a full bundle, encountered upload pipe failures, and moved to Mini. Mini validated the exact branch HEAD, built the project, and ran the changed-path suite. All 303 changed and always-run test files passed. The check then completed local validation: rendered contrast passed, UI smoke passed, the cached build was current, formatting and lint passed, and the user-docs build passed. The final check output said all checks passed.

## Approaches tried

I first reproduced only the named pressure-guard test to get a quick and specific result. It passed, which ruled out an immediate deterministic assertion failure. I then ran the required full RepoOS changed-path check rather than editing the test speculatively. RepoOS’s own retry behavior handled the hung ThinkPad and transport/cache issues, and the alternate host completed the authoritative changed-path run. I also inspected the prior review report and the worktree state so this recovery would not re-open resolved feature or foreign-bookkeeping changes.

## Challenges and blockers

The original failure report contains no assertion details beyond the test name and ThinkPad host, and this worktree’s retained local logs did not contain the remote assertion trace. The initial ThinkPad validation did not finish; RepoOS classified the container as hung. The retry encountered incremental-bundle transport problems on Bee before succeeding on Mini with a full branch snapshot. These were validation-host issues, not code failures. The final check passed, so no blocker remains for handoff.

## Key learnings

A remote test failure should be investigated at the exact test before changing unrelated production code. Here, the host-injected probe made the test independent of real network and memory readings, the focused test passed locally, and the remote environment itself later hung. RepoOS’s retry result provided stronger evidence than an unverified theory about polling: the same branch passed the complete changed-path test suite on another host. Preserve the production polling floor unless a reproducible behavioral issue demonstrates that it is wrong.
